+def within_user_ranks(user_ids, scores):
+    _, inverse = np.unique(user_ids, return_inverse=True)
+    order = np.lexsort((np.arange(len(scores)), scores, inverse))
+    sorted_groups = inverse[order]
+    starts = np.empty(len(order), dtype=np.int64)
+    boundary = np.empty(len(order), dtype=bool)
+    boundary[0] = True
+    boundary[1:] = sorted_groups[1:] != sorted_groups[:-1]
+    start_positions = np.flatnonzero(boundary)
+    group_lengths = np.diff(np.append(start_positions, len(order)))
+    starts[:] = np.repeat(start_positions, group_lengths)
+    ordinal = np.arange(len(order), dtype=np.float64) - starts
+    denominators = np.maximum(group_lengths - 1, 1)
+    ranked_sorted = ordinal / np.repeat(denominators, group_lengths)
+    singleton = np.repeat(group_lengths == 1, group_lengths)
+    ranked_sorted[singleton] = 0.5
+    ranks = np.empty(len(scores), dtype=np.float64)

Seed ensembling is the only non-dead, currently available card and can reduce variance around the unstable validation peak. However, the seven-seed expansion already slightly regressed, so the honest expected gain is below 0.002 and further expansion should be tightly bounded rather than assumed beneficial.
